title: context-document.v1
description: The complete input to one decision (A§52, plan §7 DEC-1/DEC-6). The context builder assembles it from the owning services (account, delinquency, customer, arrangement, contact) — never by reading another service's store — validates it against this schema, snapshots it to s3://colx-dev-decision-audit/input-snapshots/ and records `input_content_hash` = SHA-256 of its canonical JSON. Everything the rule engine and the models may read is here: a decision is a pure function of this document plus the pinned strategy, rule set, policy set and guardrail config, which is what makes it replayable years later. All seven sections are required — a partial context is never decided on; an upstream failure is `CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE` (fail closed), not a document with holes. The same schema shapes the batch population (`population-line.v1.json`) and the Snowflake-built context (ANA-10), and the context-parity test asserts the two are byte-identical after canonicalization.

subject.description: Who and what the decision is about.

delinquency.description: Current delinquency position of the account, owned by delinquency-service (D§5).

dpd.description: Days past due: `asOf − oldestUnpaidDueDate` in whole days, 0 when the account is current. Computed by delinquency-service, never recomputed here.

bucket.description: Delinquency bucket code from the versioned bucket configuration. Deliberately not an enum: buckets are configurable per D§5 (`GET|PUT /v1/delinquency/bucket-configs`), so a portfolio may run `CURRENT/1-30/31-60/61-90/90+` or its own ladder without a contracts change. Rules compare it with EQ/IN.

amountOverdue.description: Amount overdue in MAJOR units as a decimal string, e.g. `"500.00"` = EUR 500.00. This is the one place on the platform where money is not `int64` minor units (CLAUDE.md §3, contracts/README.md §4): collections strategies are written by business users against amounts they recognise, so a threshold reads `GT "500"` and not `GT 50000` — a rule set full of minor-unit integers is a rule set nobody proof-reads correctly. The context builder performs the minor→major conversion once (DEC-6) and the catalogue records the unit per field; the DSL compares as an exact decimal, so no float ever touches the value.

currency.description: ISO-4217 alpha-3 currency of `amountOverdue` and `account.currentBalance`. Always present with the amounts — an amount without a currency is never valid on this platform.

productCode.description: Product the account belongs to, used for product-specific treatment eligibility. Source-system code (`cb_account.prod_cd`), carried through unchanged.

currentBalance.description: Total outstanding balance in MAJOR units as a decimal string, in `delinquency.currency`. Major units for the same reason as `delinquency.amountOverdue`.

status.description: Account status as published by account-service. Not an enum here: the vocabulary is owned by that service's contract (CON-3) and this document must not fork it. Rules compare it with EQ/IN.

customer.description: Customer collection profile owned by customer-service, including the constraints that the policy stage reads first (A§54).

contactability.description: Derived contactability band (customer-service derives it so that constraints override stated preferences — plan §7 SVC-1). `UNCONTACTABLE` means no channel has usable contact details.

preferredChannel.description: Channel the customer prefers, or `NONE` when no preference is recorded. A preference is an input to optimization, never an override of policy: a preferred channel that policy forbids is still not used.

doNotContact.description: Customer-level do-not-contact flag. `true` is a policy constraint, not a preference: the policy stage suppresses every automated contact treatment and the post-selection guard re-checks it, so no optimization outcome can override it (CLAUDE.md hard rule 2, A§54).

vulnerabilityFlag.description: Customer is flagged as vulnerable or in an assistance programme (D§4.1). `true` narrows treatments to the vulnerability-safe set — a policy constraint, handled like `doNotContact`.

segment.description: Customer segment code as published by customer-service (source `segment_cd` carried through). Used by strategy eligibility and segmentation.

arrangement.description: Arrangement and promise position owned by arrangement-service — the reason most "why was this customer contacted again?" questions get answered.

hasActiveArrangement.description: An arrangement is ACTIVE (confirmed and not broken/completed). Strategies normally suppress collection contact while an arrangement is being honoured.

hasOpenPromise.description: A promise to pay is open (made, not yet due, not yet kept or broken).

brokenPromises90d.description: Count of promises broken in the last 90 days, as a whole number. Drives escalation rules: repeated broken promises usually disqualify soft treatments.

contactHistory.description: Recent contact activity owned by contact-service, and the input to frequency-cap rules. Counts are attempts recorded on the account's customer, not deliveries.

contacts7d.description: Contact attempts in the last 7 days across every channel.

contacts30d.description: Contact attempts in the last 30 days across every channel.

byChannel7d.description: Contact attempts in the last 7 days broken down by channel, e.g. `{"SMS": 1, "EMAIL": 1}`. THE ONE DELIBERATE `additionalProperties` EXCEPTION in contracts/schemas/decisioning: the key set is the channel vocabulary owned by contact-service, and a new channel there must not require a new version of every decisioning contract, so the keys are open — but not untyped. `propertyNames` constrains keys to SCREAMING_SNAKE channel codes and `additionalProperties` constrains every value to a non-negative integer count, so the map is fully typed and no free-form blob can hide here. A channel absent from the map means zero contacts on that channel; the catalogue lists the five known channels as addressable paths.

lastContactAt.description: When the most recent contact attempt was made, RFC3339 UTC with `Z`. NULL — not omitted — when the customer has never been contacted, so that a rule can test it explicitly with IS_NULL / NOT_NULL and a missing upstream is distinguishable from a genuine never-contacted.

provenance.description: Where every section of this document came from and how fresh it was — one entry per section the builder assembled (A§52, DEC-6). Required and non-empty: a decision audit that cannot say which upstream supplied `delinquency.dpd` and as of when is not an audit. Not addressable by rules (the DSL has no array quantifiers), so it never changes a decision — it only explains one.

subject.title: DecisionSubject
subject.description: The customer/account (and optionally case) a decision is about. Shared by population lines and outcome lines so the batch key and the context can be compared field for field.

customerId.description: Platform customer identifier (an unprefixed ULID in production). No pattern is imposed: dev fixtures and migration populations legitimately carry source-system keys such as `C123` (D§8), and a decision must be reproducible from the population it was made on.

accountId.description: Platform account identifier (an unprefixed ULID in production; source keys such as `A123` in fixtures and migration populations). Also the champion/challenger allocation key: the experiment bucket is derived from `accountId` + salt (testdata/allocation-golden-vectors.json), so the same account always lands in the same arm.

caseId.description: OPTIONAL — the collection case this decision belongs to, when one is open. A platform-minted ULID (unlike customerId/accountId, a case is never owned by a source system), so the envelope's ULID definition is reused rather than restated. Omitted (never null) for pre-case decisioning and for simulation populations built from history. Treatments require a case, so a TREAT decision taken without one creates the case downstream.

decimalMajorUnits.title: DecimalMajorUnits
decimalMajorUnits.description: A monetary amount in MAJOR units as a decimal string with at most two fraction digits, e.g. `"500"`, `"500.5"`, `"500.00"`, `"-12.34"`. A string rather than a JSON number so that no consumer can round-trip it through a float; negative values are permitted because credit balances and reversals exist. Valid only inside decision context documents — every other contract on the platform uses `{amountMinor: int64, currency}`.

path.description: Section or catalogue path this entry accounts for — a top-level section name (`delinquency`) covers every field beneath it; a full path (`contactHistory.contacts7d`) narrows to one field when sections come from more than one upstream.

source.description: What supplied the value: the kebab-case deployable name of the owning service for online decisions (`delinquency-service`), `snowflake-population` for batch/simulation contexts built by ANA-10, or `caller-supplied` for the role-gated TEST/SIMULATION path where the caller passes a full context.

asOf.description: As-of time of the supplied value (not the fetch time), RFC3339 UTC with `Z`. Staleness is visible in the explanation, which is how a "the data was already wrong" dispute gets settled.
